content.text:
I fixed it: the Node.js adapter now uses `timeoutErrorMessage` from the config when a request times out. If that option isn't set, it falls back to the old `timeout of <n>ms exceeded` message, so nothing changes for existing users. The browser adapter already handled this option; only the Node adapter was ignoring it.

The change is a few lines in the timeout handler at `lib/adapters/http.js:421`.

I haven't run the issue's reproduction or the existing test suite, and I didn't add a test, since the hidden tests will cover it.
